intelligence.human_view: He looked at the colors and said: less rainbow, no neon center, no rainbow-bright. Elegant, beautiful, clean, sharp. The deeper versions are better — mid to darker, not super dark, not super light. Deep emerald, deep sapphire blue, deep gold, royal purple — the real nice ones. That's the first half: depth, not brightness. The second half is sameness: the same color lightness everywhere. The same yellow on every button, the same green, the same blue, the same purple — not a whole bunch of different blues and purples and yellows, each button its own shade. One unified system. Choose the nicest of each color — the most elegant, the most beautiful, the most royal — and use THAT one everywhere, so everything looks pristine and premium. Two rules, one palette: go deep, and go once. A bright color shouts; a deep color glows. Ten different blues argue; one blue agrees with itself everywhere it appears.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine all the colors in the rainbow — but not the bright neon ones! We use the DEEP, beautiful ones instead — deep emerald green, deep sapphire blue, deep gold, royal purple — the really nice royal ones! And here's the trick: there's only ONE yellow, ONE green, ONE blue, ONE purple — the same one everywhere! Not a whole bunch of different blues and yellows all mixed up! Everything matches, like one big beautiful royal family of colors!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — imagine the colors, dear, but not the bright neon rainbow ones! We use the deep, beautiful ones — deep emerald green, deep sapphire blue, deep gold, royal purple — the really nice royal ones, love! And there's only ONE yellow, ONE green, ONE blue, ONE purple — the same one everywhere, dear! Not a whole bunch of different blues and yellows all mixed up! Everything matches, love, like one big beautiful royal family — pristine and premium!
